key_insight: The paper extends lattice Boltzmann methods to general orthogonal coordinates, enabling efficient Navier-Stokes simulation on smoothly nonuniform, clustered grids without sacrificing the collide-and-stream framework.
engineering_relevance: This makes LBM much better suited for boundary layers, multiscale flows, and other problems where local mesh refinement is needed for accuracy and computational efficiency.
method: Uses coordinate transformations to formulate LBM on general orthogonal curvilinear grids.
Derives metric-dependent equilibrium moments and geometric force terms via Chapman-Enskog analysis.
Adds correction terms for normal velocity gradients and supports multiple collision models, with central-moments MRT found most robust.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on benchmark flow problems and case studies showing significant computational advantages for boundary-layer and MHD coupled simulations on orthogonal curvilinear grids.
watch_item: Implementation is more complex than standard Cartesian LBM because the equilibria and forcing terms must be carefully adapted to local metric factors and their derivatives.
paper_title: Lattice Boltzmann Methods for Navier-Stokes Equations in General Orthogonal Coordinates for Efficient Flow Simulations using Nonuniform Clustered Grids
